comments.text: Sets up the processor and stack, silences the SID, sets the initial life digit and clears the world transition bytes before calling the quest setup.
Resets the stack and display, then tests the world transition flag. Without a transition it decrements the life digit and branches to the restart when the digit stays nonnegative.
Copies the four bytes at $4F18 into the quest setup at $173A, clears control and effect state, marks the six entries at $BF40 with $FF, and enters the main quest path at $0A44.

Selects an eight-byte disk request record by testing the transition selector and the prior-load byte at $07FF. A negative selector chooses OPEN. A nonnegative selector after the first load chooses WIN for $0A and CL otherwise.
Disables interrupts and sprites, sets the low processor-port bits to $06 and restores the working zero page from $C802-$C8FF before making the disk request.
Sets logical file 1 on device 8, sets the filename from the copied record and pushes the return address before tail-jumping to the KERNAL LOAD entry.
The selected record starts with a continuation address minus one, followed by a byte retained from the descriptor, the filename length and four padded name bytes.
Five eight-byte load descriptors in the order HL, IL, CL, WIN and OPEN. The two leading bytes are the synthetic return address for LOAD.
Byte offsets into the message group index expressed in pointers. Consecutive groups start three entries apart for the three languages.
Saves the message number in $0DDE and draws the heading selected by language $C902. It then adds the language index to a message-group offset and draws that body through the same renderer.

Walks a screen text script through $11-$12. For each segment it calculates the two screen rows and their colour addresses. It converts glyph codes to pairs of character indices, writes $9A to both rows for a space, and interprets $FE as another segment and $FF as end.
Little-endian script pointers grouped by language. The renderer uses an even byte offset computed from the requested group and language.
Screen-code scripts for the quest heading, start prompt, loading message, game over, disk-side prompts, trader and level-complete text. Segment controls are interpreted by $0E1F.
Saves A, X, Y and the port at $01, switches its low bits to $05 and acknowledges the VIC interrupt. For a raster interrupt it selects a stage address from $140E using twice the stage index at $42.
Little-endian targets for the two raster stages, $1416 and $147D.
Two raster compare values selected by the stage index, $F8 and $CB in the quest capture.

Waits until the raster passes $CD, briefly writes $7F to VIC control 1, clears the sprite X positions, switches the VIC to bank $8000 and selects the HUD bitmap and screen matrix there with $D018=$BF.
Selects VIC bank $C000 via CIA 2 and sets the screen mode and fine-scroll values from $B2 and $B4. Writes the screen and character memory selector from $B0.
Selects VIC bank $C000, sets background and sprite modes, loads two shared tile colours from the world header and selects the $F800 character set with $D018=$0F.

Uses the world start coordinates at $173A-$173D to split the starting position into metatile indices and offsets within four-character tiles. Sets up the map pointer and patches the screen and colour RAM destination operands for the initial draw.
Fetches a metatile ID from the map through $9C, subtracts one to index the two offset tables and adds the world-specific character-grid base. A zero ID uses the separate fill path.

Reads individual character codes through $62, writes them through the patched screen destination, then looks up each colour through $BC. Advances through a four-character metatile segment and stops after 40 columns.
Adds the pending digit values from $2B85 onward to the score digits at $C903, clears each pending digit and propagates a carry when the sum reaches ten.
Ticks selected active spell durations and checks the Return key when a spell is ready. Type 1 increments the life digit up to nine, while types 2 and 8 save and replace the weapon byte at $28F0.
For spell types 2 and 8 restores the previous weapon byte from $28F1 before the active state is cleared.
Drives the eight keyboard columns using $3C1E and decodes active-low row bits from CIA 1 port B using the table at $3C26. An unchanged decoded value returns zero in $3C1B.
Eight active-low masks, one per column driven on CIA 1 port A.
Eight rows of eight game key codes indexed by the scanned column and row position. A pressed entry of $FF follows the routine's continue-scanning path.
Eight rounds of shift and conditional subtraction divide the two-byte input at $46-$47 by $48. The quotient byte is written at $4A and the remainder at $4B.
Decrements Y from zero through a full 256-count loop for each outer decrement of X. X equal to zero requests 256 outer passes.
Waits until the VIC raster high bit is clear and the low raster byte equals X.
Repeats while X is greater than the current low raster byte at $D012.
Waits for the low raster counter to reach $C0, records display enable at $1414 and sets the VIC display-enable bit.
Clears the stored display-enable flag and sets border and primary background to black before clearing the VIC display-enable bit.
Preserves Y, advances the offset at $41 and reads through the indexed operand at $3CCB into $3C.
Preserves A and sets the low processor-port bits to $04 so RAM shows through the I/O window.
Preserves A and sets the low processor-port bits to $05 so the I/O window is visible.
Uses the four direction bits in $A6 to add or subtract the horizontal and vertical step sizes from the 16-bit coordinates at $79-$7A and $7D-$7E.
Takes the lowest three bits of the position on each axis, accounts for the negative-direction flags, and stores the complementary fine scroll values in $B2 and $B4 for the display stage.
Stores the within-metatile offsets in $8E and $92, shifts both 16-bit coordinates right twice, and adds the coarse column and row to the map base through the two bytes at $4F2E.
Selects character rows 0, 40, 80 and 120 within a four-row metatile stored with a stride of 40 bytes.
The exclusive end offsets used by the initial viewport draw for each four-character metatile row.
Low bytes of 190 metatile offsets into the world character grid, paired with the high bytes starting at $461E. Here map ID 1 selects entry 0.
High bytes of the character-grid offsets, paired with the low bytes at $4560.
Two little-endian world coordinates copied to $173A-$173D on a life restart before the viewport setup uses them.
Base of the colour lookup table selected at quest setup and read through zero-page pair $BC.
Base address to which the renderer adds the selected metatile’s offset from $4560 and $461E.
Base for the metatile ID grid. The viewport code adds coarse X to its low byte and coarse Y to its high byte.
Eight bytes per tile for the main multicolour character display. This world selects its tile bank with VIC bank $C000 and $D018=$0F.
